title: Headache and Pain in MS Patients and Their Impact on Daily Life Limitations - Association with Imaging Morphological Changes
summary:
Daily clinical practice shows that recurrent pain influences
treatment outcomes and is therefore considered a comorbid condition that limits treatment success. This study aims to investigate the extent to which multiple sclerosis is associated with the concurrent occurrence of pain and headaches, and how recurrent headaches and pain affect quality of life.
To this point, the relationship between headaches and pain and MS, as well as their impact on quality of life, has been insufficiently studied.
To investigate the effects of recurrent headaches and pain on treatment outcomes and quality of life, questionnaires will be administered during a structured interview to measure quality of life and limitations caused by headaches and pain. Furthermore, using MRI images obtained as part of routine care during MS clinic visits, we will investigate whether there is a correlation between morphological changes on the images and the occurrence of pain.
